Understanding
Today's Lesson
Notes:
Scripture
Memorizing
The purpose of a farmer cultivating crops is to
gather an abundant amount of crops during the harvest. To
achieve this, the farmer doesn't refuse to toil and work hard
from the beginning of spring. And finally, when the harvest
season arrives, the farmer reaps the crops with great joy and
satisfaction. However, the window of time for harvesting
grains or fruits is very short. If this time is missed, the grain
quickly fades, and shortly thereafter, storms and snowstorms
may strike. In that case, all the farmer's efforts and sacrifices
become in vain. That's why, during the harvest season,
people of all ages and genders join in to contribute to the
harvest, putting in their effort to gather even a single extra
grain.
The time we are living in is not the time for plowing the
fields, sowing seeds, or tending to the crops; it is the time for
harvesting, the season of reaping. In the Old Testament
times, the Jews and prophets plowed the fields, and the Lord
sowed the seed by giving His own life for the sins of the
world as a grain of wheat. So, from the time of His
resurrection becoming the firstfruits to His second coming is
the time of harvest. We are the harvesters of souls living in
the time to harvest the last souls of human history that God
has determined to gather people to His kingdom. The time to
harvest is running short, yet there are lazy workers who are
just sleeping and foolish laborers who do not recognize that
the harvest time is passing and are neglecting to reap the
crops. What will happen to the crops that are just waiting to
be harvested by such workers? Moreover, how would the
heart of the owner, who has already paid wages to these
workers and is waiting for them to harvest the crops, feel?
We must be aware that the quantity of harvest and the fate of
the crops that God gathers will be determined by us, who live
in the final harvest time.
And he who reaps receives wages, and gathers fruit for eternal life, that
both he who sows and he who reaps may rejoice together.
(John 4:36)

(Matthew 9:35-38)
Read John 4:28-38, and answer the following questions.
1. During His journey, Jesus became tired and weary. However, when His disciples brought food
and offered it to Jesus, He postponed eating the food. What was the reason? What kind of lesson
do you think this gives to us who are preparing for the Bible Seminar?
2. In verse 35, Jesus said “Behold, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, for they are already
white for harvest!” However, it was not the harvest season at that time. What did Jesus mean by
the harvest?
3. The Lord said that we are sent to reap what we have not worked for when we have already
received our wages. What does this mean?
- Already received our wages:
- Gathers fruit for eternal life:
4. Jesus said there is one who sows and one who reaps. Which work is easier and more enjoyable,
and which one is harder and more difficult? Why is that?

Illustration
Do It Tomorrow Morning
The steamship Central America, which was heading from New York to San
Francisco, suffered an accident in the middle of the ocean when a hole
developed in the ship's hull, causing water to enter. A passing rescue ship saw
this situation and approached SS Central America.
"Is there something wrong?" asked the captain of the rescue ship.
"There's a hole in the ship causing water to come in, and we can't perform
repairs at the moment. It's nighttime, and the passengers could also panic. The
ship will probably stay afloat until tomorrow morning, so let's observe until then
and make a decision," replied the captain of SS Central America.
With a sense of unease, the captain of the rescue ship spoke again. "Still, it
might be better to transfer the people to our ship now, considering the danger."
However, the captain of SS Central America reiterated, "Let's wait until
tomorrow morning."
Ultimately, an hour and a half later, SS Central America sank completely into
the sea, leaving no trace. Due to a negligent approach to the rescue operation in
a dire situation, they met their demise.
If you are given a chance of rescue right now, do not delay the time to accept the
gospel.
